lines.t: My son…
How long you gon’ run toward what cannot hold you?
How many crowns must break before you look up?
I was there when they hurt you.
I am here now.
I made a vow when I was young, no tears, no weak knees,
I’ma get mine, stack wins, make the whole world see.
Respect in my name, women when I walk through,
Big house, big checks, every door I talked through.
I wanted the applause like oxygen in my chest,
Told myself if they admire me, then I finally rest.
Professional killer, every goal gettin’ slain,
But the higher that I climbed, man, the colder it became.
I got what I asked for, why I still feel poor?
Why the trophies in the room feel like locks on a door?
Why the eyes that once fed me don’t feed me at all?
Why I conquer every mountain just to hate the view from tall?
You learned to survive, but you never learned peace.
You wore your wounds like armor, but I came to bring release.
You keep asking the world to name you somebody—
My son, look at Me…
Am I enough yet?
When the noise dies down, am I enough yet?
When the hands don’t clap and the crowds all leave,
When you cannot buy one breath of peace—
Am I your reality now?
Not the dream that keeps on letting you down.
Come as you are, lay the whole war down,
Am I your reality now?
I ran ahead of You, said, “I got this, let me cook,”
Tried to build a kingdom outta every wounded look.
Every “you ain’t enough” turned into gasoline,
Now I’m burnin’ through success, but it ain’t burnin’ clean.
I chased being desired, thought lust would make me whole,
But a body can’t repair what got broken in a soul.
I chased the deals, chased the rank, chased the feared reputation,
But pride is just a scared little boy in decoration.
I remember fallin’ hard, face first, no flex left,
All the things I used to worship couldn’t give me rest.
Then I heard You in the wreckage, not condemning my name,
Just a Father with His arms open wide through the shame.
I did not leave when you ran.
I did not love you because you won.
I knew the child beneath the man you built.
Come home.
YahuShua: Am I enough yet?
Son: You were enough when I could not see.
YahuShua: When the noise dies down, am I enough yet?
Son: Every false god took from me.
YahuShua: Am I your reality now?
Son: You are the truth when my world falls down.
Both: I lay the crown, I lay the war down—
You are my reality now.
I don’t need the room to turn when I enter,
I don’t need another win to remember
That I am received, I am known, I am held,
Not because of what I built, but because You never left.
I forgive that young boy tryin’ to earn love,
Tryin’ to make a father outta praise from the club.
I release the old vows: “I’ll never need nobody.”
You were beside me in the dirt; You still call me Your son.
I am not asking you to become less—
I am calling you out of the lie.
You do not have to purchase My acceptance.
You were Mine before you ever learned to strive.
Let the world keep its mirrors.
Let ambition kneel beneath love.
My Spirit is with you.
My love is enough.
YahuShua: Am I enough yet?
Son: Yes, You are enough for me.
YahuShua: Am I your reality now?
Son: You are the life inside of me.
YahuShua: When every idol hits the ground—
Son: I found the One who never turned around.
Both: No more running, no more proving somehow—
You are my reality now.
I thought I needed the world to say my name.
But You called me son…
And nothing sounds the same.
My son…
I was enough before the chase.
I am enough now.
